findings: The gate is general. Staging turns on for any lazy-init perfect HA with more than 2^16 slots, a table over 2MB, and only fixed-width payload types. It does not look at particular queries, columns or data. STRUCT, ARRAY and VARCHAR payloads are excluded by TypeIsConstantSize.

Parallel safety holds. Each flush holds stripe_locks[p]. Each staging partition matches one lock stripe because both use 2^16 slots (LARGE_PERFECT_HT_STRIPE_SIZE is now defined from STAGE_STRIPE_SIZE), and both counts are computed the same way. Neighbouring is_set bytes from different stripes are separate memory locations, so threads writing them is not a data race. The addresses/init_addresses scratch vectors and the arena belong to each thread.

State lifetime is handled. State memory comes from per-thread arenas stored in gstate.sink_allocators, which is declared before ht and therefore destroyed after it. The local HTs never set is_set, so Destroy on them does nothing. The global HT destroys every state it initialized.

Order-sensitive aggregates keep their order within a thread. The counting sort is stable, chunks are appended in arrival order, and buffers 0..used are flushed in order. FILTER columns are BOOLEAN payload columns, so they are staged and take the same payload_idx path. VectorOperations::Copy keeps NULL validity. The bounds check still runs before staging.

Every staged row is applied. Combine calls FlushStaged before returning on the shared path. Empty or no-sink local states fall through to the old CombineRange path, which is harmless. A buffer can never overflow: offset+n ≤ STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE holds after each rotation or flush.

Minor: `stage_shift` in perfect_aggregate_hashtable.hpp is unused (dead member). Also, the private per-thread table is still allocated and its is_set array memset even when the shared sink is used. This adds no new memory, but it is wasted work that a follow-up could skip.
